subject.title: Feature: Surface cron job name / session label in /status and statusline

question: Should maintainers supersede the conflicting fork PR and sponsor a narrow upstream status-label fix, or ask the fork PR author to rebase and prove the current branch?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the issue carries product/no-new-fix-pr signals and has an open conflicting linked PR, so automation should not create a second fix path without maintainer intent.

options.title: Supersede and sponsor a narrow fix
options.body: Keep this issue canonical, close or supersede the conflicting fork PR, and land an owner-reviewed fix with terminal-safe label rendering and raw-key fallback.

options.title: Ask for fork PR rebase and proof
options.body: Keep this issue open while asking the fork PR author to rebase, add sanitization, and provide real behavior proof for `/status` and TUI status output.

options.title: Defer to broader attribution design
options.body: Leave this issue open as product-direction input for the broader status/usage attribution work, accepting raw keys in CLI/TUI status for now.

recommendation.title: Supersede and sponsor a narrow fix
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical, close or supersede the conflicting fork PR, and land an owner-reviewed fix with terminal-safe label rendering and raw-key fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: The status/TUI history points most strongly to steipete for the cross-surface product and implementation-boundary decision.
